claims.text: TEEX staged the DARPA Triage Challenge at Disaster City in College Station from November 5th to November 13th.
claims.quote: The scenarios were part of the DARPA Triage Challenge, which the Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service, or TEEX, staged from Thursday, Nov. 5 through Friday, Nov. 13, at Disaster City® in College Station.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: Autonomous drones and ground robots worked alongside first responders to triage simulated mass casualty incidents and relayed critical data to human medics.
claims.quote: Autonomous drones and ground robots raced alongside first responders this week to triage simulated mass casualty incidents, spotting faux-but-lifelike life-threatening injuries and relaying critical data to human medics.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: The finals ended on November 13th at Disaster City in College Station. RoboScout won the Systems competition and $1.5 million, and Disruptors won the Data competition and $1 million.
claims.quote: The DARPA Triage Challenge concluded the Finals event on Nov. 13, 2026, at Disaster City in College Station, Texas. RoboScout won the Systems competition and $1.5 million, while Disruptors won the Data competition and $1 million.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge completes Finals event

claims.text: Competitors used autonomous systems and human machine teams in simulated disasters that included a tornado hitting an open air market, smoke, heavy darkness and complex obstacle lanes.
claims.quote: Competitors employed autonomous systems and human-machine teams to navigate simulated catastrophic events, including a tornado hitting an open air market, smoke, heavy darkness, and complex obstacle lanes.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge completes Finals event

claims.text: DARPA Director Stephen Winchell said human machine teams outperform every approach to the problem in some of the most rigorous environments.
claims.quote: We've decisively proven that human-machine teams outperform every approach to the problem in some of the most rigorous, large scale, complex environments that you've ever seen
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge completes Finals event

claims.text: Winchell then said that result was not enough.
claims.quote: But that's not enough, right?
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge completes Finals event

claims.text: Winchell said some teams did well at identifying victims and others at triage, lifesaving or evacuation.
claims.quote: Some of the teams perform really well on the identification of victims. Some of the teams perform really well on the triage and lifesaving or the evacuation pieces.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge completes Finals event

claims.text: The challenge seeks autonomous systems such as drones and robots that can assess injuries quickly, accurately and at scale in mass casualty incidents.
claims.quote: The DARPA Triage Challenge (DTC) seeks to transform how medical responders triage in mass casualty incidents (MCIs) by developing autonomous systems – such as drones and robots – that can assess injuries quickly, accurately, and at scale.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge program page

claims.text: Competing teams developed algorithms, unmanned aerial vehicles or unmanned ground vehicles designed to work with the human medics who give hands on care in the field.
claims.quote: Competing teams have developed algorithms, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and/or unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) designed to collaborate with the human medics who provide hands-on evaluation and care in the field.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge program page

claims.text: Competitors must show their systems can locate casualties, identify signs of injury and send critical data to medical response teams.
claims.quote: Through a series of scenarios, competitors must demonstrate that their systems can locate casualties, identify signs of injury, and transmit critical data to medical response teams.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge program page

claims.text: Disaster City is a 52 acre mock community with full scale structures that can collapse, rubble piles and a derailed train.
claims.quote: runs Disaster City®, a 52-acre mock community with full-scale structures that can collapse, rubble piles, a derailed train and more to simulate realistic disaster response in a simulated and safe environment.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: More than 100 participants from the U.S. military, universities, tech companies and startups competed for more than $3 million in cash prizes.
claims.quote: more than 100 participants from the U.S. military, universities, tech companies and startups competed for over $3 million in cash prizes
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: Teams were graded at DARPA's command post, where computing technology checked every mock casualty report against each patient's simulated injuries and vital signs.
claims.quote: Teams are graded by DARPA’s command post, where state-of-the-art computing technology checks every mock casualty report against each patient’s simulated injuries and vital signs.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: The five competitions included a simulated tornado ripping through a community market, smoke filled buildings, nighttime searches in near darkness and search and rescue under rubble.
claims.quote: Each of the five competitions was unique, including a simulated tornado ripping through a community market, smoke-filled buildings, nighttime searches in near darkness and search and rescue under piles of rubble.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: Moulage artists made hyper realistic mock injuries for the challenge.
claims.quote: Behind the scenes at the DARPA Triage Challenge, skilled moulage artists create hyper-realistic mock injuries.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground (photo caption)

claims.text: For the Human Machine Teaming course each team was assigned medics, and teams and medics worked together to rapidly triage casualties.
claims.quote: Teams are assigned medics they will partner with for the Human-Machine Teaming (HMT) course, in which teams and medics work together to rapidly triage casualties.
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: Program manager Jeremy Pamplin said the challenge was built to be the most realistic, repeatable and rigorous testbed for assessing medical technologies ever created.
claims.quote: We did this challenge to be the most realistic, repeatable and rigorous testbed for assessing medical technologies ever created
claims.document: TEEX, TEEX turns Disaster City into a DARPA Triage Challenge proving ground

claims.text: Competitors used the technology their teams developed to read vital signs from a distance and work alongside human medics.

claims.text: DARPA has an open SBIR topic, TRIAGE-X, for autonomous medical triage systems that recognize chemical toxidromes and physically deliver the antidote or a life saving intervention.
claims.quote: If you’d like to get involved, DARPA has an open SBIR topic, TRIAGE-X, which seeks to develop and demonstrate capability with autonomous medical triage systems to recognize chemical toxidromes and physically deliver the corresponding antidote or life-saving intervention.
claims.document: DARPA, DARPA Triage Challenge completes Finals event

claims.text: DARPA says the TRIAGE-X topic is open until November 25th, 2026.
claims.quote: is open until Nov. 25, 2026.

claims.quote: For retired U.S. Army Col. and physician Jeremy Pamplin, program manager for the DARPA Triage Challenge, choosing TEEX was an easy decision.

claims.text: Points from each competition decided which teams reached the championship round, where the top two teams competed for the $1.5 million grand prize.

rejected.reason: None of the three pages uses the term. They say algorithms, autonomous systems and autonomous medical triage systems (c8, c9, c19). No copy may call them AI.
